java_model: PSystemCommandFactory.getCandidate asks each registered command to validate the current line. An OK_PARTIAL command receives successive physical lines through isMultilineCommandOk until that same command returns OK or NOT_OK, so the command owns its interior before later commands are considered.
CommandMultilines2 validates the first line with the command-specific starting regex and the last line with the command-specific END regex. Interior lines are not offered as sibling commands.

CommandFactoryNote accepts floating aliases matching [%pLN_.]+ and its END is ^[%s]*end[%s]?note$, so a dot is valid in an alias and one whitespace character, including a tab, is valid between end and note.
CommandFactoryNoteOnEntity has distinct ordinary and final-bracket commands. The ordinary command ends only with end-note syntax; the bracket command ends only with a closing brace.

FactorySequenceNoteCommand accepts optional ampersand parallel and slash vertical-merge prefixes before note, hnote, or rnote. Its END deliberately permits note, hnote, or rnote regardless of opener shape.
rust_model: bf402b56 centralizes opener recognition in note_command_parts and span discovery in completed_multiline_note_payload, then adds independent class, deployment, and sequence buffering paths.

note_command_parts strips ampersand and slash prefixes, but SeqParser::try_note still begins its consumer regex at (h|r)?note. Dispatch therefore hides prefixed bodies while the sequence consumer rejects the opener and later parses body words as participants.

completed_multiline_note_payload uses is_note_family_terminator for every non-brace opener. That matches Java sequence semantics but is broader than Java CommandFactoryNote and CommandFactoryNoteOnEntity, where hnote/rnote endings remain ordinary payload.

is_ordinary_note_terminator accepts only endnote and end note after trimming. It does not implement Java's single-whitespace END regex, so a tab-terminated Java-valid block remains unterminated in Rust.

ClassParser's floating multiline regex restricts aliases to a single word even though Java accepts dotted aliases. The shared dispatch helper recognizes the command, but the selected class consumer drops it.

The deployment multiline floating regex accepts an optional color non-capturingly, NoteAccum has no color field, DeploymentNote has no color field, and render_floating_deployment_note always uses NOTE_FILL. The command is retained after f1378066, but its color semantics are discarded.

f1378066 changes floating deployment note source-line retention, layout membership, emission order, and rendering. It does not repair alias, terminator, sequence-prefix, or note-color grammar/model gaps.

fresh_perturbations.detail: Rust retains and orders the note after f1378066, but discards its MistyRose color and renders the default note fill. A 0.01 vertical coordinate difference also remains, but the color mismatch alone rejects command construction parity.
Java renders the parallel hexagonal note. Rust dispatch recognizes the prefixed opener, but SeqParser rejects it; body words become extra participants and the note disappears.
Java parses and vertically merges the rectangular note. Rust rejects the slash-prefixed opener, omits the note, and creates participants from its body.
SVGs are structurally equivalent; Java sequence commands intentionally permit a different note-family END.
Java's [%s]? END regex accepts the tab and renders the note plus later class. Rust recognizes neither the completed span nor the parser terminator and emits only its minimal empty envelope.

findings: The account's core causal claim is supported: Java gives an OK_PARTIAL command exclusive ownership of physical lines until that exact command's END regex accepts the block.

The implementation does not preserve that exact-command boundary. It replaces command-specific END regexes with a shared family predicate, which is correct for sequence notes but overbroad for ordinary class and attached notes.

Dispatch and consumer grammars are not one model. Prefixes are stripped for span discovery but rejected by SeqParser, dotted aliases are recognized as note commands but rejected by ClassParser, and Java-valid tab termination is accepted by neither Rust layer.
Deployment floating-note lifecycle is now present, but command construction remains lossy because the accepted color is not represented in NoteAccum or DeploymentNote.
No fixture-shaped shipping logic, golden-data read, filename conditional, or unexplained parity constant was found in the reviewed implementation.

The preserved multiple-floating-note class case still fails only in SVEK placement. It is retained and reported as an explicit out-of-scope renderer residue, not counted as a parser-mechanism failure.
Six fresh valid counterexamples directly reject the implementation across terminator specificity, whitespace grammar, alias grammar, sequence prefixes, and deployment note metadata.
verdict_reason: Rejected. Although every previously identified parser counterexample except the separately-accounted multiple-floating-note layout case now compares structurally, six fresh Java-valid inputs disprove exact command atomicity. Rust overgeneralizes ordinary-note END matching, omits Java's whitespace terminator grammar, splits dispatch recognition from consumer grammar for dotted aliases and sequence prefixes, and discards accepted deployment note color metadata.
